steps.tx: **Chronic lymphocytic leukaemia** CLL is defined by a clonal B-lymphocyte count of 5 x 10^9/L or higher in peripheral blood co-expressing CD5, CD19, CD20, and CD23 with weak surface immunoglobulin. Flow cytometry demonstrates clonality via light-chain kappa or lambda restriction. Smudge cells or basket cells are characteristically prominent on peripheral blood films due to mechanical fragility of mature neoplastic lymphocytes.

rows: Essential hallmark of CLL and Mantle cell
Negative in marginal zone and follicular
Dim CD20 distinguishes CLL from normal B cells
Bright surface Ig typical of non-CLL lymphomas

steps.tx: The smear shows crowded **small mature lymphocytes** with dense clumped chromatin scattered among red cells. Their fragile membranes rupture during slide making, leaving the pale crushed **smudge cell** visible near the center. Flow markers noted on the image include CD5 with CD19 and CD23 plus weak surface immunoglobulin. This **clonal B cell** pattern defines chronic lymphocytic leukaemia and separates it from other lymphomas.
steps.say: The blood film is packed with small mature lymphocytes showing dark clumped chromatin, typical of chronic lymphocytic leukaemia. One fragile cell has smeared during spreading, forming a classic smudge cell. The labeled profile of CD5 with CD19 and CD23 plus weak surface immunoglobulin confirms a single clone. Recognizing this combination on smear and flow testing establishes the diagnosis and points away from other B cell disorders.

vis.alt: The smear shows many small mature lymphocytes with clumped chromatin plus a crushed smudge cell.
vis.caption: Blood film displays classic leukemic lymphocytes and a smudge cell. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Molecular cytogenetics provides fundamental risk stratification. **TP53 aberrations** 17p deletion and TP53 mutation and unmutated IGHV status confer aggressive disease course and chemoimmunotherapy resistance. Deletion 17p assessed by FISH or somatic TP53 mutations abolishes DNA damage-induced apoptosis, rendering alkylators and purine analogs largely ineffective and mandating targeted pathway inhibitors regardless of disease stage.

right.title: Favourable Genomic Features
points: Absence of TP53, ATM, or NOTCH1 mutations
Indolent disease course and prolonged survival

steps.tx: Clinical staging stratifies disease burden and determines when treatment is indicated. CLL staging utilizes **Rai** and Binet systems based on lymphocytosis, lymphadenopathy, organomegaly, anaemia haemoglobin under 10 or 11 g/dL, and thrombocytopenia platelets under 100 x 10^9/L. Rai intermediate or Binet B disease with active symptoms, or Rai stage III/IV and Binet C with marrow failure, warrants prompt initiation of therapy.

rows: Lymphocytosis only in blood and marrow

steps.tx: Targeted B-cell receptor pathway blockade has revolutionized therapeutic standards. **Bruton tyrosine kinase** BTK inhibitors ibrutinib, acalabrutinib, and zanubrutinib establish superior progression-free survival over chemoimmunotherapy across frontline and relapsed CLL. Second-generation inhibitors acalabrutinib and zanubrutinib demonstrate reduced off-target inhibition of TEC and EGFR kinases, significantly diminishing atrial fibrillation, bleeding, and hypertensive toxicities.

rows: Significantly less atrial fibrillation and hypertension
Superior PFS over ibrutinib in relapsed/refractory CLL

steps.tx: Fixed-duration targeted combinations eradicate minimal residual disease. Time-limited frontline **venetoclax** plus obinutuzumab for 12 months demonstrates significant progression-free and overall survival superiority over chlorambucil-obinutuzumab in the CLL14 trial. In CLL14, high rates of undetectable minimal residual disease in peripheral blood and bone marrow translated into sustained treatment-free remission without continuous lifelong drug exposure.

steps.tx: Aggressive histological transformation represents an acute clinical emergency. **Richter transformation** describes the rapid clinicopathological transformation of CLL into an aggressive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma in 2% to 10% of patients, carrying poor prognosis. Patients manifest sudden B symptoms, asymmetrical rapid lymphadenopathy, and precipitous LDH rises. FDG PET-CT showing SUVmax over 5 directs targeted excisional biopsy.

left.title: Chronic Lymphocytic Leukaemia
points: Managed with targeted BTK or BCL-2 inhibitors

right.title: Richter Transformation (DLBCL)
points: High-grade diffuse sheets of large transformed B-cells
Rapid clinical deterioration with constitutional symptoms
Treated with R-CHOP chemoimmunotherapy or CAR-T

steps.tx: The node section contrasts dark clusters of small **CLL cells** with broad sheets of large transformed cells effacing the architecture, labeled as **DLBCL transformation**. This matters because **Richter transformation** in the lesson marks an aggressive shift with sudden symptoms and rising LDH, confirmed by targeted biopsy of avid disease and managed as large cell lymphoma.
steps.say: The image shows a lymph node with residual dark small lymphocytes beside sweeping sheets of much larger transformed cells that efface normal structure. It reinforces the lesson warning that rapid nodal growth with systemic symptoms and rising markers signals transformation, confirmed by biopsy of the most active site and treated as aggressive lymphoma.

vis.alt: The node section shows small dark lymphocytes beside sheets of large transformed cells.
vis.caption: Node section contrasting small lymphocytes with large transformed sheets Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Immune dysregulation causes non-malignant cytopenias secondary to host immune dysfunction. **Autoimmune complications** in CLL include autoimmune haemolytic anaemia AIHA with positive direct antiglobulin test and immune thrombocytopenic purpura ITP, managed with corticosteroids. When autoimmune cytopenias fail systemic prednisone or dexamethasone, rituximab, intravenous immunoglobulin, or thrombopoietin receptor agonists provide effective secondary rescue without needing cytotoxic escalation.

steps.tx: Distinct mature B-cell neoplasms display unique clinicopathological and genomic markers. **Hairy cell leukaemia** is an indolent B-cell neoplasm marked by pancytopenia, splenomegaly, dry bone marrow tap, and ubiquitous BRAF V600E mutations, exquisitely sensitive to cladribine. Phase microscopy reveals circumferential cytoplasmic hairy projections, with flow cytometry confirming CD11c, CD25, CD103, and annexin A1 expression.
